Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 20-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Augmented and Virtual Reality [CSE_4051]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                An automobile company is developing a Virtual Reality car showroom that allows customers to             (5)  
  explore vehicles, change colors, and experience interior designs virtually.  
  A)           Explain with a diagram how the five classic components of a VR system interact to deliver an  
  immersive and responsive virtual showroom experience.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           A gaming studio observes how Virtual Reality has evolved from early experimental systems to a           (5)  
  major segment of the entertainment industry.  
  i) Analyze how advancements in hardware design, realistic content creation, and interactive user  
  interfaces have driven this growth.  
  ii) Discuss the major technical or user-experience limitations that still restrict VR gaming from wider  
  adoption.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                An educational institution plans to host 100 students in a shared VR classroom with interactive 3D      (5)  
  models.  
  A)           Apply suitable VR environment optimization methods and recognition techniques for the 4 gesture  
  types to ensure real-time performance and student engagement.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           An AR-based maintenance platform assists factory technicians by overlaying 3D repair instructions (5)  
  on machines in real time.  
  i) Analyze how combining visual and haptic feedback enhances accuracy and reduces training  
  errors.  
  ii) Evaluate how gesture and voice input interfaces improve task efficiency compared to traditional  
  handheld controllers.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                A VR ocean exploration simulator uses multimodal outputs to create a realistic deep-sea                 (5)  
  environment.  
  A)           Apply VR output design techniques to enhance immersion and user experience.  
  i) Apply suitable lighting, depth cues, and graphics rendering to improve underwater distance  
  judgment and visibility in low-light ocean environments.  
  ii) Apply 3D spatial sound techniques to help users detect and localize marine life and  
  environmental cues (e.g., sonar pings, whale calls).  
  iii) Apply haptic feedback mechanisms such as vibration and resistance forces to simulate water  
  Page #1

pressure and motion while swimming or interacting with objects underwater.  
  iv) Apply VR display performance requirements (wide FOV, lightweight headset, accurate motion  
  tracking, low latency) to maintain comfort, prevent disorientation, and ensure synchronized  
  multisensory feedback.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         An AR fashion design studio allows designers to visualize, modify, and simulate virtual garments in (5)  
  real time.  
  i) Analyze how geometric modeling defines garment structure, shape, and fit when applied to  
  different body models.  
  ii) Evaluate how behavioral modeling simulates realistic cloth motion using physics-based  
  properties such as flexibility, elasticity, and draping behavior, including inverse kinematics for  
  adapting to user movement in real time.  
  iii) Analyze how texture mapping and advanced visual rendering techniques enhance perception of  
  fabric color, shine, and pattern under varied lighting conditions.  
  iv) Analyze how model management techniques maintain consistency among geometric changes,  
  fabric behavior, and visual updates during continuous garment editing in AR.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)              A multi-camera infrared tracking system needs to find the 3D position of markers from images         (5)  
  captured by two calibrated cameras.  
  A)         i) Apply blob detection and epipolar constraint to explain how the system identifies and matches the  
  correct marker points between the two camera images.  
  ii) Apply triangulation to describe how the matched 2D points are used to estimate the 3D marker  
  position.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         A VR architectural walkthrough requires both realistic lighting and smooth motion, but the current          (5)  
  system drops below 30 fps during navigation.  
  i) Analyze the impact of using different lighting and shading models on the realism vs.  
  computational cost trade-off.  
  ii) Discuss how the geometry and rasterization stages (projection, clipping, Z-buffering, double  
  buffering) ensure correctness and stability of the final visual output.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)              A VR training simulator requires a virtual metallic hammer to look shiny and produce realistic impact (5)  
  when striking a surface.  
  A)         Apply the concepts of physical property modeling and physics-based behavior modeling to explain  
  how the hammer's visual properties and physical properties will be defined to achieve realism.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         In a VR firefighting training simulation, a firefighter avatar must react realistically while interacting   (5)  
  with a burning environment.  
  The simulation uses physics-based behavior modeling (for fire heat, object collision, hose  
  movement) and AI behavior (for responding fire dynamics and trapped civilians).  
  i) Analyze how physics-based behavior and AI-driven behavior must work together to create  
  believable training outcomes.  
  ii) Explain what would go wrong if either physics or AI behavior is inaccurately modeled.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
